status: predeclared; physical-model approval and forward verification pending

selection.active: Among unselected targets, maximize the final active fraction.
selection.demanding: Among unselected targets, maximize the weighted mean square of the saved source control.
selection.ties: Choose the smallest zero-based query index.
selection.outcome_policy: Retain every selected case and every attempted forward termination status.

source_policy.source: Saved control array; never recover a replacement from a changed operator.
source_policy.units: W/m^3 = stored control * oil_conductivity_W_m_K * temperature_scale_K / length_scale_m^2
source_policy.space: P1 nodal field, zero extension at inlet Dirichlet nodes; original nodal mass-lumped loading at the optimization resolution.
source_policy.refinement: Evaluate this same P1 field on nested meshes. Report source-integral and disabled-feedback discretization changes.
source_policy.time: Right-slab piecewise constant on (t[n-1],t[n]], with stored slab n applied throughout that interval.
source_policy.initial_temperature: Use the saved optimization initial condition.
source_policy.target: Use the original analytic desired-temperature function at assessment time levels.

comparisons: computed flow with thermal feedback disabled
computed flow with thermal feedback enabled

proposed_feedback.model: axisymmetric laminar incompressible Navier-Stokes with Boussinesq forcing
proposed_feedback.thermal_coefficients: Keep the optimization coefficients and background heat sources unchanged.
proposed_feedback.momentum_properties: Require density, dynamic viscosity, expansion coefficient, reference temperature and a traceable property source before application runs.
proposed_feedback.scope: A single-feedback sensitivity assessment with frozen transport properties. Its physical suitability requires a property-variation and flow-regime check.

verification.uncertainty: Report spatial and temporal differences separately. A failed resolution target leaves the physical comparison unresolved.
